front: TC002: What is the minimum viable move?
back: Before saying “That happened to me too”, say one support line first: “That sounds like a lot — what happened next?”

front: TC002: What is the core sequence?
back: Notice the shift impulse → support their thread → invite one more detail → share only if it adds value → return to them. -> Short form: notice → respond → invite → calibrate → release. -> “That sounds rough — what part went wrong?” then actually listen before you relate. -> “I’ve been there too, but yours sounds like the bigger story. What happened?” -> “That’s a big one. What was the best bit?” — support the win before you match it..

front: TC002: What is the field tip?
back: Support first, relate second, return the floor.

front: TC002: What is the strong version of: Same thing happened to me. (Shifts straight to yourself and can feel like a hijack.)?
back: I’ve got a related story, but yours sounds like the important bit. What was the turning point? (Names the reciprocity while protecting their moment.)

front: TC002: What is the strong version of: Oh, I did that last year. (Turns their win into your anecdote.)?
back: That’s brilliant. What was the best part for you? I’ve done something similar, but I want to hear yours first. (Support, invite, then reciprocity.)

front: TC002: What is the strong version of: You think that’s bad, let me tell you about my week. (Competes with their stress.)?
back: That sounds genuinely hard. Talk me through it — I won’t turn it into my own saga. (Support with a light, honest reassurance.)

front: TC002: What is better than: “Oh, the same thing happened to me…”?
back: “That sounds rough — what happened?” (your story can come later)

front: TC002: What is better than: “Mm. And then? … And then?” with nothing of your own?
back: “That makes sense. I’ve had a version of that too — here’s the bit that helped.”

front: TC002: What is better than: “Where? Who? Why? And then what?”?
back: “Sounds like the Q&A was the real problem.” (reflect rather than interrogate)

front: TC002: What are signs it is working?
back: They add more detail after your support line. Their tone relaxes rather than tightens. They keep going on the same thread instead of trailing off. They eventually ask for your related experience. They move from bare facts into how it actually felt. They say “exactly”, “yeah”, or “that’s the thing”. The exchange feels easier, not more self-conscious.

front: TC002: When should you avoid this technique?
back: The other person directly asks about your experience The conversation has clearly moved into mutual exchange

front: TC002: What is the best recovery line?
back: “Actually, your bit is the important one here — what happened next?”
